title: Marine Engineer Salary: Award Rates, Hourly Conversion, and Annual Pay Guide
description: Understand marine engineer salary under the Seagoing Industry Award 2020. Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay, including overtime, super, and tax for 2026-27.
salarySummary: A marine engineer's aggregate annual salary under the award ranges from $97,737 (third engineer) to $132,272 (master), based on a 70-hour week for 27 weeks per year, but typical full-time hours average 55 hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the hourly rate for a marine engineer under the Seagoing Industry Award?
faqs.a: The award does not set a simple hourly rate because pay is aggregated to include overtime. For a chief engineer on a dry cargo vessel up to 19,000 tonnes (AOV), the aggregate annual salary is $126,997. Based on the award’s assumed 70-hour week over 27 weeks, the effective hourly rate is about $67.20. However, if you divide the minimum weekly rate of $1,718.80 by 38 ordinary hours, the base hourly rate is $45.23, with overtime paid separately. Always check the specific classification and vessel manning.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a marine engineer?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of the salary at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026-27). For a chief engineer earning $126,997 aggregate, the super contribution would be $15,239.64 per year, provided the ordinary earnings component does not exceed the cap. The employer must make these contributions to avoid the super guarantee charge.

faqs.q: Do marine engineers receive casual loading?
faqs.a: Marine engineers are typically employed full-time or on relief contracts, not casual. If a marine engineer were engaged as a casual employee, the 25% casual loading would apply on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $45.23 per hour, the casual rate would be $56.54 per hour. However, casual loading is uncommon in the seagoing industry; most roles are permanent or fixed-term.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Marine Engineer Salary

If you are researching a **marine engineer salary** in Australia, the most reliable sources are the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Seagoing Industry Award 2020 and data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics. Unlike many occupations where pay is quoted as an hourly rate, marine engineers are often paid an aggregate annual salary that includes overtime, penalty rates, and allowances. This guide explains how to convert that salary into an hourly equivalent, what a typical fortnight looks like, and how tax and super apply.

### The Award Framework

The Seagoing Industry Award 2020 sets minimum pay for marine engineers based on classification and vessel manning. For example, a chief engineer on a dry cargo vessel of up to 19,000 tonnes (AOV) receives an aggregate annual salary of **$126,997**. This figure is calculated on the basis of 10 hours per day, 70 hours per week, for 27 weeks of the year (the typical work pattern at sea). The award also provides a minimum weekly rate for full-time employees: for a chief engineer, that is **$1,718.80 per week**.

To find the hourly rate from the weekly figure, divide by 38 ordinary hours: $1,718.80 ÷ 38 = **$45.23 per hour**. However, this base rate does not include the overtime that is built into the aggregate salary. The aggregate salary already accounts for two hours of overtime per day at 200% and additional weekend work. For a more realistic hourly comparison, divide the aggregate annual salary by the actual hours worked. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, marine engineers work an average of **55 hours per week** full-time. Using that figure: $126,997 ÷ (55 × 52) ≈ **$44.40 per hour**. This is close to the base rate, confirming that the aggregate salary fairly compensates the long hours.

### Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

The standard formula used on this site is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a marine engineer earning $45.23 per hour and working 38 hours per week (the standard assumption for most occupations), the annual salary would be $45.23 × 38 × 52 = **$89,374**. But this understates the true pay because marine engineers work many more hours and receive overtime. The award’s aggregate salary of $126,997 is the correct figure for a chief engineer. If you are offered an hourly rate, use the formula with your expected weekly hours. For example, at $50 per hour and 55 hours per week: $50 × 55 × 52 = **$143,000**.

### The Fortnightly View

Pay for marine engineers is often paid monthly (clause 15.1 of the award), but you can calculate a fortnightly equivalent by dividing the annual salary by 26. For the chief engineer: $126,997 ÷ 26 = **$4,884.50 per fortnight**. If you are paid weekly, divide by 52: **$2,442.25 per week**. These figures help when budgeting or comparing with other jobs that pay fortnightly.

### Tax and Superannuation

For the 2026-27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office’s resident tax rates apply:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (using the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds as a guide). For a chief engineer earning $126,997, the tax estimate is roughly $30,067 plus Medicare, leaving about $94,430 after tax. This is before any salary packaging or HELP repayments.

Superannuation is paid on top of the salary at **12% of ordinary earnings**, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For $126,997, the super contribution is $15,239.64. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer. You can read more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) on our site.

### Casual Loading and Other Considerations

Marine engineers are rarely casual, but if you are engaged as a casual employee, the 25% casual loading applies on top of the base hourly rate. For the chief engineer base rate of $45.23, the casual rate would be $56.54 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it.

### Comparing with Other Occupations

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. A marine engineer’s award rate is significantly higher, reflecting the specialised skills and demanding work conditions. The ABS reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70, so a marine engineer’s aggregate salary of $126,997 ($2,442 per week) is above the national average. For more comparisons, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures, including estimated tax and super. Remember to enter your base rate without casual loading already included—the checkbox adds it for you. This is useful for marine engineers who want to see how a shore-based hourly rate compares with their seagoing salary.

### Summary

A **marine engineer salary** is best understood through the award’s aggregate annual figures, which account for the long hours and overtime typical at sea. The base hourly rate from the weekly minimum is around $45.23, but actual earnings are much higher due to the 55-hour average work week. Use the formula hourly × hours × 52 to convert any offer, and always check the specific classification and vessel type. For further reading, see our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page.
